newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche 96 net profit grew 4.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche 96 net profit grew 4.8 pct.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, on Tuesday reported a 4.8 percent rise in net profit to 2.2 billion marks ($1.3 billion) in 1996 and said operating profit jumped 37 percent to 5.8 billion marks.
The net profit lags earnings growth at Deutsche's major domestic rivals but was at the upper end of analysts' forecasts. The operating profit was above expectations.
Deutsche's shares responded by rising to a twelve-month high of 87.70 marks in early electronic trade, up 0.60 marks or 0.7 percent from Monday's close.
Analysts had expected net profit would be stagnant or show only minor growth due to a series of blows to Deutsche's earnings last year.
The bank was hit by the estimated 200 million-pound ($323 million) cost of compensating investors for alleged mismanagement at three unit trusts run by London-based Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.
But analysts expected little direct impact on earnings because Deutsche was expected to have used some reserves to foot the bill.
The MGAM affair, which came to light last September, was only the latest in a string of problems.
The bank is estimated to have added more than 200 million marks to risk provisions to cover a bail-out of engineering group Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG (KHD).

Also, two major shareholdings, Daimler-Benz AG and construction group Philipp Holzmann AG, omitted dividends for 1995, costing Deutsche 219 million marks in lost income, according to analysts' estimates.
In a brief statement, Deutsche said its balance sheet total jumped 23 percent to 886 billion marks in 1996 due to increased trading activities as part of its expanding investment banking business.
The loan volume rose by 8.2 percent to 410 billion marks while customer deposits grew by 25 percent to 375 billion marks.
--David Crossland, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 0.619 British Pounds) ($ = 1.702 German Marks)
